finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so the authorization check is never enforced. Any caller can delete any account. closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete, which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user (non-admin, non-owner) sending DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id
finding.sink: accounts.remove(id) at AccountService.java:23, which deletes an account the user does not own

trace.note: Entry point: DELETE /accounts/{id}; the id is attacker-controlled
Account loaded by the attacker-supplied id with no ownership scoping
canDelete(u, a) returns a boolean that is ignored; no throw or early return on false

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) is correct but unused here. assertCanDelete (13-17) would enforce it but is not called in deleteAccount. No other auth layer, filter or middleware exists in the repo (only this one source file). Compare closeAccount (27-31), which does enforce the check.

verdict.guard_found: none effective: canDelete (lines 9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) throws but is only called in closeAccount (line 29). No other auth layer exists in the repo (only src/AccountService.java).
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 the boolean from canDelete(u, a) is a bare statement with no throw or return, so accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any authenticated non-owner, non-admin caller, unlike closeAccount, which calls assertCanDelete at line 29.
